complexity_scope.guarantee: Per-instance expectation over directions. No high-probability, last-iterate or uniform sample-path claim.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The bound retains the explicit factor (n+4)^2, bias coefficient 1 and factor 1/2 in (45), and factor 4 in (46). No claim of unrestricted optimality is made.
complexity_scope.oracle: Two exact function values per estimator at x_k and x_k+mu u_k, arbitrary R^n value access, exact projection onto Q, iid standard Gaussian sampling.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Expected gap E[f(hat{x}_N)-min_Q f] for the best measured iterate among x0,...,xN; (45) also bounds the displayed deterministic weighted sum of expected iterate gaps.
complexity_scope.regime: General inequality: n>=1, N>=0 integer, mu>0 and deterministic h_k>0, global convex L0-Lipschitz f with attained constrained minimum. Accuracy tuning additionally requires epsilon,L0,R>0 and the radius promise.
complexity_scope.resource: The inclusive k=0,...,N implementation uses at most 2(N+1) exact value calls, N+1 projections and N+1 Gaussian-vector draws; selection reuses the base values and uses at most N comparisons. Projection and sampling costs are charged separately. Accuracy tuning has order n^2 L0^2 R^2/epsilon^2 for this selected method.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected finite-value RS_mu with B=I and best-iterate output; an Algorithm-specific upper bound only.

content.intended_use: Certify the source finite-value RS_mu guarantee under its global convex Lipschitz assumptions.

proofs.locator: PDF pp16–17 Proof of Theorem 6; p16 best-iterate inequality; pp7–9 smoothing identities; p12 Theorem 4(1); pp36–37 selected Appendix proofs
map: Source prerequisites: f_mu is convex and f_mu>=f by p7 (11). The gradient identity (21), pp8–9, gives E[g_mu(x,u)]=grad f_mu(x). Theorem 4(1), p12 (34), gives E||g_mu(x,u)||^2<=L0^2(n+4)^2; its nonsmooth Proof uses |f(x+mu u)-f(x)|<=mu L0||u|| and Lemma 1's fourth-moment upper bound (17).
Theorem 1, p8 (18), gives |f_mu(x)-f(x)|<=mu L0 sqrt(n). Its C^{0,0} Proof on p37 bounds the smoothing integral by mu L0 M_1 and uses M_1<=sqrt(n). Lemma 1's moment Proof was read on pp36–37.

The source Proof on pp16–17 sets r_k=||x_k-x*||. Projection gives r_{k+1}^2<=r_k^2-2h_k<g_mu(x_k,u_k),x_k-x*>+h_k^2||g_mu(x_k,u_k)||^2. Conditioning on the history, using (21), (34), convexity of f_mu and f_mu(x_k)>=f(x_k), yields E_{u_k}r_{k+1}^2<=r_k^2-2h_k(f(x_k)-f_mu(x*))+h_k^2(n+4)^2L0^2.

The source then takes expectation over the earlier directions. Sum this recurrence for k=0,...,N, including the deterministic k=0 start. Dropping the nonnegative terminal expected squared distance gives 2 sum h_k(phi_k-f_mu(x*))<=||x0-x*||^2+(n+4)^2L0^2 sum h_k^2. Using f_mu(x*)<=f*+mu L0 sqrt(n) and dividing by 2S_N is exactly (45). This spells out the telescope referred to by the source Proof; it is not a new transfer theorem.

The best-iterate comparison on p16 is pointwise: f(hat{x}_N)<=sum h_k f(x_k)/S_N for positive steps. The paragraph before (46), p17, applies this output to RS_mu. Thus (45) gives the same bound for its expected gap. The displayed steps balance the two terms in the distance/moment fraction, and (46) supplies the stated epsilon tuning.

assumptions: f:R^n->R is finite and convex, and |f(x)-f(y)|<=L0||x-y|| for every x,y in R^n with a finite L0>=0.
Q is closed and convex and a constrained minimizer x* exists; the starting point x0 in Q is fixed.
mu>0 is fixed, and h_0,...,h_N are prescribed positive deterministic finite real numbers.
u_k are iid N(0,I_n), independent of the previous history. The estimator uses exact f values on all of R^n, and the update uses exact Euclidean projection.
A radius bound ||x0-x*||<=R is needed only for the accuracy-tuned corollary, not for inequality (45).
statement.conclusion: Theorem 6 (45): (1/S_N) sum_{k=0}^N h_k(phi_k-f*) <= mu L0 sqrt(n) + [||x0-x*||^2+(n+4)^2 L0^2 sum_{k=0}^N h_k^2]/(2S_N). The source best-iterate output satisfies E[f(hat{x}_N)-f*] <= the same right-hand side. As stated after the Proof and in (46), choosing 0<mu<=epsilon/(2L0 sqrt(n)), h_k=R/((n+4)L0 sqrt(N+1)), and an integer horizon N=ceil(4(n+4)^2 L0^2 R^2/epsilon^2) ensures E[f(hat{x}_N)-f*]<=epsilon. The ceiling is explicit implementation rounding of the source's displayed real-valued horizon. No weighted-average output extension is claimed.
statement.objects_and_definitions: E=R^n with ordinary Euclidean norm (the paper's B=I specialization). Q is a nonempty closed convex subset. f*=min_{x in Q}f(x)=f(x*) for a fixed minimizer x* in Q. For mu>0 let f_mu(x)=E_{u~N(0,I_n)}f(x+mu u), g_mu(x,u)=[f(x+mu u)-f(x)]u/mu. Set x_{k+1}=proj_Q(x_k-h_k g_mu(x_k,u_k)), S_N=sum_{k=0}^N h_k, phi_0=f(x0), and phi_k=E_{u_0,...,u_{k-1}}f(x_k) for k>=1. Let hat{x}_N be a best function-value iterate among x0,...,xN.
statement.parameter_domains: n is an integer >=1; N is an integer >=0; 0<mu<infinity; 0<h_k<infinity for 0<=k<=N; 0<=L0<infinity. For the accuracy-tuned corollary require epsilon>0, L0>0, R>0 and ||x0-x*||<=R.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible f,Q,x0,x*,mu and positive deterministic step sequence, and for every integer N>=0, the stated bound holds. Expectations are over the independently sampled Gaussian directions; this is a per-instance expectation guarantee. The best-iterate output depends only on u_0,...,u_{N-1} and its queried values.
